+fn strip_ansi(text: &str) -> String {
+    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
+    let mut chars = text.chars();
+    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
+        if c == '\u{1b}' {
+            if chars.next() == Some('[') {
+                for next in chars.by_ref() {
+                    if ('@'..='~').contains(&next) {
+                        break;
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            continue;
+        }
+        out.push(c);
+    }
+    out

44	fn scan_tree(dir: &Path, findings: &mut Vec<String>) {
45	    let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(dir) else {
46	        return;
47	    };
48	    for entry in entries.flatten() {
49	        let path = entry.path();
50	        let name = entry.file_name();
51	        let name = name.to_string_lossy();
52	        if path.is_dir() {
53	            if name == "target" || name == ".git" || name == "node_modules" {
54	                continue;
55	            }
56	            scan_tree(&path, findings);
57	        } else if path
58	            .extension()
59	            .and_then(|ext| ext.to_str())
60	            .is_some_and(|ext| TEXT_EXTENSIONS.contains(&ext))
61	            || name.ends_with(".sh")
62	            || !name.contains('.')
63	        {
64	            scan_file(&path, findings);
65	        }

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-09 19:36:27Z)**_

I've read every changed file and traced each new sink/source. Summary of why I'm not raising findings:

- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`**: Adds `cargo test --workspace --locked` to release-verify. This is a *strengthening* of the gate (tests now actually run). The step accesses no secrets (none injected via `env:`), and the job is gated by `needs.release-policy.outputs.build_artifacts == 'true'`, which release-trust.mjs sets only on real release lanes — not on arbitrary PR pushes. No CI/CD trust regression.

- **`crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs`** & **`src/prompt.rs`**: Both edits are entirely inside `#[cfg(test)]` modules and only swap an `"\x1b…"` literal for `format!("{esc}…", esc = char::from(27))`. Same bytes, same behavior, no runtime/shipped surface affected.

- **`crates/deadreckon/tests/chain.rs`**: The new util-linux branch passes a shell command to `script -c`: `format!("{} chain --draft --from-stdin", env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_deadreckon"))`. `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*` is a cargo-controlled compile-time constant pointing at the target dir — not attacker-influenceable at runtime. Test-only code; no production sink. The `strip_ansi` helper is test-only and operates on a `&str` captured from the child's stdout/stderr — pure transformation, no sink.

- **`crates/deadreckon/tests/coherence.rs`**: Changes `take(35)` to `take(45)` for a README-content assertion. Doc-layout test only.

- **`crates/deadreckon/tests/portability.rs`**: `match … { Ok(e) => e, Err(_) => return }` → `let Ok(e) = … else { return };`. Identical semantics. The surrounding scan still fails-closed on read errors (the function is a guard that flags hardcoded developer paths; a read failure simply means nothing to scan, which is the same as before).

No source→sink path with attacker influence was introduced.
